option.name: --http-header-fields-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --http-header-fields-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --http-proxy
tip: URL of the HTTP/HTTPS proxy.
If this is set, the http_proxy environment is ignored.
The no_proxy environment variable is still respected.
This option is silently ignored if it does not start with http://.
Proxies are not used for https URLs.
Setting this option does not try to make the ytdl script use the proxy.

option.name: --hue
tip: Adjust the hue of the video signal (default: 0).
You can get a colored negative of the image with this option.
Not supported by all video output drivers.

option.name: --hwdec
tip: Specify the hardware video decoding API that should be used if possible.
Whether hardware decoding is actually done depends on the video codec.
If hardware decoding is not possible, mpv will fall back on software decoding.
(default no)

option.name: --hwdec-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --hwdec-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --hwdec-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --hwdec-codecs
tip: Allow hardware decoding for a given list of codecs only.
The special value all always allows all codecs.
(default h264,vc1,hevc,vp8,vp9,av1,prores,prores_raw,ffv1,dpx)

option.name: --hwdec-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --hwdec-extra-frames
tip: Number of GPU frames hardware decoding should preallocate (default: see --list-options output).
If this is too low, frame allocation may fail during decoding, and video frames might get dropped and/or corrupted.
Setting it too high simply wastes GPU memory and has no advantages.

option.name: --hwdec-image-format
tip: Set the internal pixel format used by hardware decoding via --hwdec (default no).
The special value no selects an implementation specific standard format.
Most decoder implementations support only one format, and will fail to initialize if the format is not supported.

option.name: --hwdec-pre
tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --hwdec-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --hwdec-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --hwdec-threads
tip: Number of threads used for hardware decoding (default: 4).
This, as opposed to vd-queue, enables frame and slice threading in libavcodec.
It can help with pipelining the decoding process and improve performance.
The exact behavior depends on the hardware decoder API used.

option.name: --hwdec-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --icc-3dlut-size
tip: Size of the 3D LUT generated from the ICC profile in each dimension.
The default of auto means to pick the size automatically based on the profile characteristics.
Sizes may range from 2 to 512.

option.name: --icc-cache
tip: Store and load 3DLUTs created from the ICC profile on disk in the cache directory (Default: yes).
This can be used to speed up loading, since LittleCMS 2 can take a while to create a 3D LUT.
Note that these files contain uncompressed LUTs.
Their size depends on the --icc-3dlut-size, and can be very big.

option.name: --icc-cache-dir
tip: The directory where icc cache is stored.
Cache is stored in the system's cache directory (usually ~/.cache/mpv) if this is unset.

option.name: --icc-force-contrast
tip: Override the target device's detected contrast ratio by a specific value.
This is detected automatically from the profile if possible, but for some profiles it might be missing, causing the contrast to be assumed as infinite.
As a result, video may appear darker than intended.
If this is the case, setting this option might help.
This only affects BT.1886 content.
The default of no means to use the profile values.
The special value inf causes the BT.1886 curve to be treated as a pure power gamma 2.4 function.

option.name: --icc-intent
tip: Specifies the ICC intent used for the color transformation (when using --icc-profile).
(default 1)

option.name: --icc-profile
tip: Load an ICC profile and use it to transform video RGB to screen output.
Needs LittleCMS 2 support compiled in.
This option overrides the --target-prim, --target-trc and --icc-profile-auto options.

option.name: --icc-profile-auto
tip: Automatically select the ICC display profile currently specified by the display settings of the operating system.
(default no)

option.name: --icc-use-luma
tip: Use ICC profile luminance value. (Only for --vo=gpu-next)
(default no)

option.name: --idle
tip: Makes mpv wait idly instead of quitting when there is no file to play.
Mostly useful in input mode, where mpv can be controlled through input commands. (Default: no)

option.name: --ignore-path-in-watch-later-config
tip: Ignore the path when matching watch-later config entries.

option.name: --image-display-duration
tip: If the current file is an image, play the image for the given amount of seconds (default: 5). inf means the file is kept open forever (until the user stops playback manually).

option.name: --image-exts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --image-exts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --image-exts-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --image-exts-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --image-exts-pre
tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --image-exts-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --image-exts-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --image-exts-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --image-lut
tip: Specifies a custom LUT file (in Adobe .cube format) to apply to the colors during image decoding.
The exact interpretation of the LUT depends on the value of --image-lut-type. (Only for --vo=gpu-next)

option.name: --image-lut-type
tip: Controls the interpretation of color values fed to and from the LUT specified as --image-lut.
Possible values: auto, native, normalized, conversion.
(default auto)

option.name: --image-subs-hdr-peak
tip: Controls the image subtitle diffuse white level in cd/m² (nits) for HDR output (default: sdr). sdr is 203 cd/m² for standard SDR white, while video uses video metadata. (--vo=gpu-next only)

option.name: --image-subs-video-resolution
tip: Override the image subtitle resolution with the video resolution (default: no).
Normally, the subtitle canvas is fit into the video canvas (e.g. letterboxed).
Setting this option uses the video size as subtitle canvas size.
Can be useful to test broken subtitles, which often happen when the video was transcoded, while attempting to keep the old subtitles.

option.name: --include
tip: Specify configuration file to be parsed after the default ones.

option.name: --index
tip: Controls how to seek in files.
Note that if the index is missing from a file, it will be built on the fly by default, so you don't need to change this.
But it might help with some broken files.
Possible values: default, recreate.

option.name: --initial-audio-sync
tip: When starting a video file or after events such as seeking, mpv will by default modify the audio stream to make it start from the same timestamp as video, by either inserting silence at the start or cutting away the first samples.

Disabling this option makes the player behave like older mpv versions did: video and audio are both started immediately even if their start timestamps differ, and then video timing is gradually adjusted if necessary to reach correct synchronization later.

option.name: --input-ar-delay
tip: Delay in milliseconds before we start to autorepeat a key (default: 200).
Set it to 0 to disable.

option.name: --input-ar-rate
tip: Number of key presses to generate per second on autorepeat (default: 40).

option.name: --input-builtin-bindings
tip: Enable loading of built-in key bindings during start-up (default: yes).
This option is applied only during (lib)mpv initialization, and if disabled then it will not be not possible to enable them later.
May be useful to libmpv clients.

option.name: --input-builtin-dragging
tip: Enable the built-in window-dragging behavior (default: yes).
Setting it to no disables the built-in dragging behavior.
Note that unlike the window-dragging option, this option only affects VOs which support the begin-vo-dragging command, and does not disable window dragging initialized with the command.

option.name: --input-cmdlist
tip: Prints all commands that can be bound to keys.

option.name: --input-commands
tip: Define a list of commands for mpv to run.
The syntax is the same as format as input.conf but without the key binding argument at the beginning.
When this option is set at startup, the commands will run after audio and video playback are about to begin if applicable (in idle mode with no file, it will run immediately).
When changing values at runtime, the commands will also run as soon as possible.

option.name: --input-commands-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --input-commands-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --input-commands-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --input-commands-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --input-commands-pre
tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --input-commands-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --input-commands-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --input-commands-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --input-conf
tip: Specify input configuration file other than the default location in the mpv configuration directory (usually ~/.config/mpv/input.conf).

option.name: --input-cursor
tip: Permit mpv to receive pointer events reported by the video output driver.
Necessary to use the OSC.
Support depends on the VO in use.
(default yes)

option.name: --input-cursor-passthrough
tip: Tell the backend windowing system to allow pointer events to passthrough the mpv window.
This allows windows under mpv to instead receive pointer events as if the mpv window was never there.
(default no)

option.name: --input-default-bindings
tip: Enable default-level ("weak") key bindings (default: yes).
These are bindings which config files like input.conf can override.
It currently affects the builtin key bindings, and keys which scripts bind using mp.add_key_binding (but not mp.add_forced_key_binding because this overrides input.conf).

option.name: --input-doubleclick-time
tip: Time in milliseconds to recognize two consecutive button presses as a double-click (default: 300).

option.name: --input-dragging-deadzone
tip: Begin the built-in window dragging when the mouse moves outside a deadzone of N pixels while the mouse button is being held down (default: 3).
This only affects VOs which support the begin-vo-dragging command.

option.name: --input-ime
tip: Enable keyboard input via an active input method (IME) connected to the VO. (default: no).
The input popup window, if there is any, is always positioned at the top left of the window.
Whether pre-edit text is drawn depends on the platform.
You may need to configure your IME to display the pre-edit inside of the input popup window if you cannot read the pre-edit text in the mpv window.

option.name: --input-ipc-client
tip: Connect a single IPC client to the given FD.
This is somewhat similar to --input-ipc-server, except no socket is created, and instead the passed FD is treated like a socket connection received from accept().
In practice, you could pass either a FD created by socketpair(), or a pipe.
In both cases, you must make sure that the FD is actually inherited by mpv (do not set the POSIX CLOEXEC flag).

option.name: --input-ipc-server
tip: Enable the IPC support and create the listening socket at the given path.

option.name: --input-key-fifo-size
tip: Specify the size of the FIFO that buffers key events (default: 7).
If it is too small, some events may be lost.

The main disadvantage of setting it to a very large value is that if you hold down a key triggering some particularly slow command then the player may be unresponsive while it processes all the queued commands.

option.name: --input-keylist
tip: Prints all keys that can be bound to commands.

option.name: --input-media-keys
tip: On systems where mpv can choose between receiving media keys or letting the system handle them - this option controls whether mpv should receive them.
(default yes)

option.name: --input-preprocess-wheel
tip: Preprocess WHEEL_* events so that while scrolling on the horizontal or vertical direction, the events aren't generated for another direction even when the two directions are scrolled together (default: yes).

option.name: --input-right-alt-gr
tip: (macOS and Windows only) Use the right Alt key as Alt Gr to produce special characters.
If disabled, count the right Alt as an Alt modifier key.
Enabled by default.

option.name: --input-tablet-emulate-mouse
tip: Emulate mouse move and button presses for tablet events (default: yes).

option.name: --input-terminal
tip: --input-terminal=no prevents the player from reading key events from standard input.
Useful when reading data from standard input.
This is automatically enabled when - is found on the command line.

There are situations where you have to set it manually, e.g. if you open /dev/stdin (or the equivalent on your system), use stdin in a playlist or intend to read from stdin later on via the loadfile or loadlist input commands.
(default yes)

option.name: --input-test
tip: Input test mode.
Instead of executing commands on key presses, mpv will show the keys and the bound commands on the OSD.
Has to be used with a dummy video, and the normal ways to quit the player will not work (key bindings that normally quit will be shown on OSD only, just like any other binding).
See INPUT.CONF.
(default no)

option.name: --input-touch-emulate-mouse
tip: When multi-touch support is enabled (either required by the platform, or enabled by --native-touch), emulate mouse move and button presses for the touch events (default: yes).
This is useful for compatibility for mouse key bindings and scripts which read mouse positions for platforms which do not support --native-touch=no (e.g. Wayland).

option.name: --input-vo-keyboard
tip: Disable all keyboard input on for VOs which can't participate in proper keyboard input dispatching.
May not affect all VOs.
Generally useful for embedding only.
(default yes)

option.name: --interpolation
tip: Reduce stuttering caused by mismatches in the video fps and display refresh rate (also known as judder).
(default no)

option.name: --interpolation-preserve
tip: Preserve the previous frames' interpolated results even when renderer parameters are changed - with the exception of options related to cropping and video placement, which always invalidate the cache.
Enabling this option makes dynamic updates of renderer settings slightly smoother at the cost of slightly higher latency in response to such changes.
Defaults to on. (Only affects --vo=gpu-next, note that --vo=gpu always invalidates interpolated frames)

option.name: --interpolation-threshold
tip: Threshold below which frame ratio interpolation gets disabled (default: 0.01).

This is calculated as abs(disphz/vfps - 1) < threshold, where vfps is the speed-adjusted video FPS, and disphz the display refresh rate. (The speed-adjusted video FPS is roughly equal to the normal video FPS, but with slowdown and speedup applied.
This matters if you use --video-sync=display-resample to make video run synchronously to the display FPS, or if you change the speed property.)

option.name: --inverse-tone-mapping
tip: If set, allows inverse tone mapping (expanding dynamic range).
Can be used for upscaling SDR content to HDR, or for making HDR content brighter.
Not supported by all tone mapping curves.
Use with caution. (--vo=gpu-next only)
(default no)

option.name: --js-memory-report
tip: Enable memory reporting for javascript scripts in the stats overlay.
This is disabled by default because it has an overhead and increases memory usage.
This option will only work if it is enabled before mpv is started.

option.name: --keep-open
tip: Do not terminate when playing or seeking beyond the end of the file, and there is no next file to be played (and --loop is not used).
Instead, pause the player.
When trying to seek beyond end of the file, the player will attempt to seek to the last frame.
(default no)

option.name: --keep-open-pause
tip: If set to no, instead of pausing when --keep-open is active, just stop at end of file and continue playing forward when you seek backwards until end where it stops again.
Default: yes.

option.name: --keepaspect
tip: --keepaspect=no will always stretch the video to window size, and will disable the window manager hints that force the window aspect ratio. (Ignored in fullscreen mode.)
(default yes)

option.name: --keepaspect-window
tip: --keepaspect-window=yes (the default) will lock the window size to the video aspect. --keepaspect-window=no disables this behavior, and will instead add black bars if window aspect and video aspect mismatch.
Whether this actually works depends on the VO backend. (Ignored in fullscreen mode.)

option.name: --lavfi-complex
tip: Set a "complex" libavfilter filter, which means a single filter graph can take input from multiple source audio and video tracks.
The graph can result in a single audio or video output (or both).

option.name: --length
tip: Stop after a given time relative to the start time.
See --start for valid option values and examples.
(default none)

option.name: --libplacebo-opts
tip: Passes extra raw option to the libplacebo rendering backend (used by --vo=gpu-next).
May override the effects of any other options set using the normal options system.
Requires libplacebo v6.309 or higher.
Included for debugging purposes only.

option.name: --libplacebo-opts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --libplacebo-opts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --libplacebo-opts-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --libplacebo-opts-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --libplacebo-opts-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --libplacebo-opts-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --linear-downscaling
tip: Scale in linear light when downscaling.
It should only be used with a --fbo-format that has at least 16 bit precision.
This option has no effect on HDR content.
Enabled by default.

option.name: --linear-upscaling
tip: Scale in linear light when upscaling.
Like --linear-downscaling, it should only be used with a --fbo-format that has at least 16 bits precisions.
This is not usually recommended except for testing/specific purposes.
Users are advised to either enable --sigmoid-upscaling or keep both options disabled (i.e. scaling in gamma light).
(default no)

tip: Prints all available options.

option.name: --list-properties
tip: Print a list of the available properties.
(default no)

option.name: --list-protocols
tip: Print a list of the supported protocols.

option.name: --load-auto-profiles
tip: Enable the builtin script that does auto profiles (default: auto).
See Conditional auto profiles for details. auto will load the script, but immediately unload it if there are no conditional profiles.

option.name: --load-commands
tip: Enable the built-in script to enter commands in the console (default: yes).
The key is used to activate this by default.

option.name: --load-context-menu
tip: Enable the builtin script that implements a context menu.
Defaults to yes on platforms where integration with a native context menu is not implemented, and to no on platform where it is.

option.name: --load-osd-console
tip: Enable the built-in script to handle textual input (default: yes).
(deprecated alias: --load-osd-console)

option.name: --load-positioning
tip: Enable the builtin script that provides various keybindings to pan videos and images (default: yes).

option.name: --load-scripts
tip: If set to no, don't auto-load scripts from the scripts configuration subdirectory (usually ~/.config/mpv/scripts/). (Default: yes)

option.name: --load-select
tip: Enable the builtin script that lets you select from lists of items (default: yes).
By default, its keybindings start with the g key.

option.name: --load-stats-overlay
tip: Enable the builtin script that shows useful playback information on a key binding (default: yes).
By default, the i key is used (I to make the overlay permanent).

option.name: --load-unsafe-playlists
tip: Load URLs from playlists which are considered unsafe (default: no).
This includes special protocols and anything that doesn't refer to normal files.
Local files and HTTP links on the other hand are always considered safe.

option.name: --log-file
tip: Opens the given path for writing, and print log messages to it.
Existing files will be truncated.
The log level is at least -v -v, but can be raised via --msg-level (the option cannot lower it below the forced minimum log level).

option.name: --loop-file
tip: Loop a single file N times. inf means forever, no means normal playback.
For compatibility, --loop-file and --loop-file=yes are also accepted, and are the same as --loop-file=inf.
(default no)

option.name: --loop-playlist
tip: Loops playback N times.
A value of 1 plays it one time (default), 2 two times, etc. inf means forever. no is the same as 1 and disables looping.
If several files are specified on command line, the entire playlist is looped. --loop-playlist is the same as --loop-playlist=inf.

option.name: --lut
tip: Specifies a custom LUT (in Adobe .cube format) to apply to the colors as part of color conversion.
The exact interpretation depends on the value of --lut-type. (Only for --vo=gpu-next)

option.name: --lut-type
tip: Controls the interpretation of color values fed to and from the LUT specified as --lut.
Possible values: auto, native, normalized, conversion.
(default auto)

option.name: --mc
tip: Maximum A-V sync correction per frame (in seconds)
(default -1)

option.name: --media-controls
tip: (Windows only) Enable integration of media control interface SystemMediaTransportControls.
(default yes)

option.name: --merge-files
tip: Pretend that all files passed to mpv are concatenated into a single, big file.
This uses timeline/EDL support internally.
(default no)

option.name: --metadata-codepage
tip: Codepage for various input metadata (default: auto).
This affects how file tags, chapter titles, etc. are interpreted.
In most cases, this merely evaluates to UTF-8 as non-UTF-8 codepages are obscure.

option.name: --mf-fps
tip: Framerate used when decoding from multiple PNG or JPEG files with mf:// (default: 1).

option.name: --mf-type
tip: Input file type for mf:// (available: jpeg, png, tga, sgi).
By default, this is guessed from the file extension.

option.name: --monitoraspect
tip: Set the aspect ratio of your monitor or TV screen.
A value of 0 disables a previous setting (e.g. in the config file).
Overrides the --monitorpixelaspect setting if enabled.
(default 0)

option.name: --monitorpixelaspect
tip: Set the aspect of a single pixel of your monitor or TV screen (default: 1).
A value of 1 means square pixels (correct for (almost?) all LCDs).
See also --monitoraspect and --video-aspect-override.

option.name: --msg-color
tip: Enable colorful console output on terminals (default: yes).

option.name: --msg-level
tip: Control verbosity directly for each module.
The all module changes the verbosity of all the modules.
The verbosity changes from this option are applied in order from left to right, and each item can override a previous one.

option.name: --msg-module
tip: Prepend module name to each console message.
(default no)

option.name: --msg-time
tip: Prepend timing information to each console message.
The time is in seconds since the player process was started (technically, slightly later actually), using a monotonic time source depending on the OS.
This is CLOCK_MONOTONIC on sane UNIX variants.
(default no)

option.name: --mute
tip: Set startup audio mute status (default: no).

option.name: --native-fs
tip: (macOS only) Uses the native fullscreen mechanism of the OS (default: yes).

option.name: --native-keyrepeat
tip: Use system settings for keyrepeat delay and rate, instead of --input-ar-delay and --input-ar-rate (default: no).
Whether this applies depends on the VO backend and how it handles keyboard input.
Does not apply to terminal input.

option.name: --native-touch
tip: (Windows only) For platforms which send emulated mouse inputs for touch-unaware clients, such as Windows, use system native touch events, instead of receiving them as emulated mouse events (default: no).
This is required for multi-touch support for these platforms.

option.name: --network-timeout
tip: Specify the network timeout in seconds (default: 60 seconds).
This affects at least HTTP.
The special value 0 uses the FFmpeg defaults.
If a protocol is used which does not support timeouts, this option is silently ignored.

option.name: --on-all-workspaces
tip: (X11 and macOS only) Show the video window on all virtual desktops.
(default no)

option.name: --ontop
tip: Makes the player window stay on top of other windows.
(default no)

option.name: --ontop-level
tip: (macOS only) Sets the level of an on-top window (default: window).

option.name: --opengl-check-pattern-a
tip: Integer option.
(default 0)

option.name: --opengl-check-pattern-b
tip: Integer option.
(default 0)

option.name: --opengl-early-flush
tip: Call glFlush() after rendering a frame and before attempting to display it (default: auto).
Can fix stuttering in some cases, in other cases probably causes it.

The auto mode will call glFlush() only if the renderer is going to wait for a while after rendering, instead of flipping GL front and backbuffers immediately (i.e. it doesn't call it in display-sync mode).

option.name: --opengl-es
tip: Controls which type of OpenGL context will be accepted:
Possible values: auto, yes, no.
(default auto)

option.name: --opengl-glfinish
tip: Call glFinish() before swapping buffers (default: disabled).
Slower, but might improve results when doing framedropping.
Can completely ruin performance.
The details depend entirely on the OpenGL driver.

option.name: --opengl-pbo
tip: Enable use of PBOs.
On some drivers this can be faster, especially if the source video size is huge (e.g. so called "4K" video).
On other drivers it might be slower or cause latency issues.
(default no)

option.name: --opengl-rectangle-textures
tip: Force use of rectangle textures (default: no).
Normally this shouldn't have any advantages over normal textures.
Note that hardware decoding overrides this flag.
Could be removed any time.

option.name: --opengl-swapinterval
tip: Interval in displayed frames between two buffer swaps.
1 is equivalent to enable VSYNC, 0 to disable VSYNC.
Defaults to 1 if not specified.

option.name: --opengl-waitvsync
tip: Call glXWaitVideoSyncSGI after each buffer swap (default: disabled).
This may or may not help with video timing accuracy and frame drop.
It's possible that this makes video output slower, or has no effect at all.

option.name: --orawts
tip: Copies input pts to the output video (not supported by some output container formats, e.g. AVI).
In this mode, discontinuities are not fixed and all pts are passed through as-is.
Never seek backwards or use multiple input files in this mode!
(default no)

option.name: --ordered-chapters
tip: Enable support for Matroska ordered chapters. mpv will load and search for video segments from other files, and will also respect any chapter order specified for the main file (default: yes).

option.name: --ordered-chapters-files
tip: Loads the given file as playlist, and tries to use the files contained in it as reference files when opening a Matroska file that uses ordered chapters.
This overrides the normal mechanism for loading referenced files by scanning the same directory the main file is located in.

option.name: --oremove-metadata
tip: Specifies metadata to exclude from the output file when copying from the input file.

option.name: --oremove-metadata-del

option.name: --oremove-metadata-pre
tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

tip: Whether to load the on-screen-controller (default: yes).

option.name: --osd-align-x
tip: Control to which corner of the screen OSD should be aligned to (default: left).

option.name: --osd-align-y
tip: Vertical position (default: top).
Details see --osd-align-x.

option.name: --osd-bar
tip: Enable display of the OSD bar (default: yes).

option.name: --osd-bar-align-x
tip: Position of the OSD bar. -1 is far left, 0 is centered, 1 is far right.
Fractional values (like 0.5) are allowed.
(default 0)

option.name: --osd-bar-align-y
tip: Position of the OSD bar. -1 is top, 0 is centered, 1 is bottom.
Fractional values (like 0.5) are allowed.
(default 0.5)

option.name: --osd-bar-h
tip: Height of the OSD bar, in percentage of the screen height (default: 3.125).

option.name: --osd-bar-marker-min-size
tip: Minimum OSD bar marker size.
(default 1.6)

option.name: --osd-bar-marker-scale
tip: Factor for the OSD bar marker size relative to the OSD bar outline size.
(default 1.3)

option.name: --osd-bar-marker-style
tip: Set the OSD bar marker style.
(default triangle)

option.name: --osd-bar-outline-size
tip: Size of the outline of the OSD bar in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
(default 0.5)

option.name: --osd-bar-w
tip: Width of the OSD bar, in percentage of the screen width (default: 75).
A value of 50 means the bar is half the screen wide.

option.name: --osd-bitmap-max-size
tip: Set the maximum bitmap cache size in libass cache for the OSD.
0 means libass uses its default value.
This accepts values in MB.

option.name: --osd-blur
tip: Gaussian blur factor applied to the OSD font border.
0 means no blur applied (default).

option.name: --osd-bold
tip: Format text on bold.
(default no)

option.name: --osd-border-style
tip: See --sub-border-style.
Style used for OSD text border.
(default outline-and-shadow)

option.name: --osd-color
tip: Specify the color used for OSD.
See --sub-color for details.
(default #FFFFFFFF)

option.name: --osd-duration
tip: Set the duration of the OSD messages in ms (default: 1000).

option.name: --osd-font
tip: Specify font to use for OSD.
The default is sans-serif.

option.name: --osd-font-provider
tip: See --sub-font-provider for details and accepted values.
Note that unlike subtitles, OSD never uses embedded fonts from media files.
Possible values: auto, none, fontconfig.
(default auto)

option.name: --osd-font-size
tip: Specify the OSD font size.
See --sub-font-size for details.
(default 30)

option.name: --osd-fonts-dir
tip: See --sub-fonts-dir for details.
Defaults to ~~/fonts.

option.name: --osd-fractions
tip: Show OSD times with fractions of seconds (in millisecond precision).
Useful to see the exact timestamp of a video frame.
(default no)

option.name: --osd-glyph-limit
tip: Set the maximum number of cached glyphs in libass cache for the OSD.
0 means libass uses its default value.

option.name: --osd-italic
tip: Format text on italic.
(default no)

option.name: --osd-justify
tip: Choices: auto left center right option.
Possible values: auto, left, center, right.
(default auto)

option.name: --osd-level
tip: Specifies which mode the OSD should start in.
(default 1)

option.name: --osd-margin-x
tip: Left and right screen margin for the OSD in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
(default 16)

option.name: --osd-margin-y
tip: Top and bottom screen margin for the OSD in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
(default 16)

option.name: --osd-msg1
tip: Show this string as message on OSD with OSD level 1 (visible by default).
The message will be visible by default, and as long as no other message covers it, and the OSD level isn't changed (see --osd-level).
Expands properties; see Property Expansion.

option.name: --osd-msg2
tip: Similar to --osd-msg1, but for OSD level 2.
If this is an empty string (default), then the playback time is shown.

option.name: --osd-msg3
tip: Similar to --osd-msg1, but for OSD level 3.
If this is an empty string (default), then the playback time, duration, and some more information is shown.

option.name: --osd-on-seek
tip: Set what is displayed on the OSD during seeks.
The default is bar.

option.name: --osd-outline-color
tip: See --sub-color.
Color used for the OSD font outline.
(default #FF000000)

option.name: --osd-outline-size
tip: Size of the OSD font outline in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
A value of 0 disables outlines.
(default 1.65)

option.name: --osd-playing-msg
tip: Show a message on OSD when playback starts.
The string is expanded for properties, e.g. --osd-playing-msg='file: ${filename}' will show the message file: followed by a space and the currently played filename.

option.name: --osd-playing-msg-duration
tip: Set the duration of osd-playing-msg in ms.
If this is unset, osd-playing-msg stays on screen for the duration of osd-duration.
(default 0)

option.name: --osd-playlist-entry
tip: Whether to display the media title, filename, or both.
If the media-title is not available, it will display only the filename.
(default title)

option.name: --osd-prune-delay
tip: Set the delay for automatic pruning of events from memory in libass.
Disabled by default.
See also --sub-ass-prune-delay.

option.name: --osd-scale
tip: OSD font size multiplier, multiplied with --osd-font-size value.
(default 1)

option.name: --osd-scale-by-window
tip: Whether to scale the OSD with the window size (default: yes).
If this is disabled, --osd-font-size and other OSD options that use scaled pixels are always in actual pixels.
The effect is that changing the window size won't change the OSD font size.

option.name: --osd-selected-color
tip: The color of the selected item in lists.
See --sub-color for details.
(default #FFFABD2F)

option.name: --osd-selected-outline-color
tip: The outline color of the selected item in lists.
See --sub-color for details.
(default #FF000000)

option.name: --osd-shadow-color
tip: See --sub-color.
Color used for OSD text background.
(default #AF000000)

option.name: --osd-shadow-offset
tip: Displacement of the OSD shadow in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
A value of 0 disables shadows.
(default 0)

option.name: --osd-shaper
tip: Set the text layout engine used by libass for the OSD.
Default: complex.
See also --sub-shaper

option.name: --osd-spacing
tip: Horizontal OSD/sub font spacing in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
This value is added to the normal letter spacing.
Negative values are allowed.
(default 0)

option.name: --osd-status-msg
tip: Show a custom string during playback instead of the standard status text.

This overrides the status text used for --osd-level=3, when using the show-progress command (by default mapped to P), and when seeking if enabled with --osd-on-seek or osd- prefixes in input.conf (see Input Command Prefixes).
Expands properties.
See Property Expansion.

option.name: --oset-metadata
tip: Specifies metadata to include in the output file.
Supported keys vary between output formats.
For example, Matroska (MKV) and FLAC allow almost arbitrary keys, while support in MP4 and MP3 is more limited.

option.name: --oset-metadata-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --oset-metadata-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --oset-metadata-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --oset-metadata-del

option.name: --oset-metadata-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --oset-metadata-set

option.name: --ovc
tip: Specifies the output video codec.
See --ovc=help for a full list of supported codecs.

option.name: --ovcopts
tip: Specifies the output video codec options for libavcodec.
See --ovcopts=help for a full list of supported options.

option.name: --ovcopts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --ovcopts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --ovcopts-clr

option.name: --ovcopts-remove

option.name: --ovcopts-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --override-display-fps
tip: Set the display FPS used with the --video-sync=display-* modes.
By default, a detected value is used.
Keep in mind that setting an incorrect value (even if slightly incorrect) can ruin video playback.
On multi-monitor systems, there is a chance that the detected value is from the wrong monitor.
(deprecated alias: --override-display-fps)

option.name: --panscan
tip: Enables pan-and-scan functionality (cropping the sides of e.g. a 16:9 video to make it fit a 4:3 display without black bands).
The range controls how much of the image is cropped.
May not work with all video output drivers.
(default 0)

option.name: --pause
tip: Start the player in paused state.
(default no)

option.name: --pipewire-buffer
tip: Set the audio buffer size in milliseconds.
A higher value buffers more data, and has a lower probability of buffer underruns.
A smaller value makes the audio stream react faster, e.g. to playback speed changes.
"native" lets the sound server determine buffers.
(default native)

option.name: --pipewire-remote
tip: Specify the PipeWire remote daemon name to connect to via local UNIX sockets.
An empty <remote> string uses the default remote named pipewire-0.

option.name: --pipewire-volume-mode
tip: Specify if the ao-volume property should apply to the channel volumes or the global volume.
By default the channel volumes are used.

option.name: --pitch
tip: Raise or lower the audio's pitch by the factor given as parameter.
Does not affect playback speed.
Playing with an altered pitch automatically inserts the scaletempo2 audio filter.
(default 1)

option.name: --play-direction
tip: Control the playback direction (default: forward).
Setting backward will attempt to play the file in reverse direction, with decreasing playback time.
If this is set on playback starts, playback will start from the end of the file.
If this is changed at during playback, a hr-seek will be issued to change the direction.
(deprecated alias: --play-dir)

option.name: --player-operation-mode
tip: For enabling "pseudo GUI mode", which means that the defaults for some options are changed.
This option should not normally be used directly, but only by mpv internally, or mpv-provided scripts, config files, or .desktop files.
See PSEUDO GUI MODE for details.

option.name: --playlist
tip: Play files according to a playlist file.
Supports some common formats.
If no format is detected, it will be treated as list of files, separated by newline characters.
You may need this option to load plaintext files as a playlist.
Note that XML playlist formats are not supported.

option.name: --playlist-exts
tip: Playlist file extensions to try to match when using --autocreate-playlist or --directory-filter-types.
(default cue,edl,m3u,m3u8,pls)

option.name: --playlist-exts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --playlist-exts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --playlist-exts-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --playlist-exts-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --playlist-exts-pre
tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --playlist-exts-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --playlist-exts-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --playlist-exts-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --playlist-start
tip: Set which file on the internal playlist to start playback with.
The index is an integer, with 0 meaning the first file.
The value auto means that the selection of the entry to play is left to the playback resume mechanism (default).
If an entry with the given index doesn't exist, the behavior is unspecified and might change in future mpv versions.
The same applies if the playlist contains further playlists (don't expect any reasonable behavior).
Passing a playlist file to mpv should work with this option, though.
E.g. mpv playlist.m3u --playlist-start=123 will work as expected, as long as playlist.m3u does not link to further playlists.

option.name: --prefetch-playlist
tip: Prefetch next playlist entry while playback of the current entry is ending (default: no).
This merely opens the URL of the next playlist entry as soon as the current URL is fully read.

option.name: --profile
tip: Use the given profile(s), --profile=help displays a list of the defined profiles.

option.name: --profile-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --profile-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --profile-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --profile-del

tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --profile-remove

option.name: --profile-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --profile-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --pulse-allow-suspended
tip: Allow mpv to use PulseAudio even if the sink is suspended (default: no).
Can be useful if PulseAudio is running as a bridge to jack and mpv has its sink-input set to the one jack is using.

option.name: --pulse-buffer
tip: Set the audio buffer size in milliseconds.
A higher value buffers more data, and has a lower probability of buffer underruns.
A smaller value makes the audio stream react faster, e.g. to playback speed changes.
"native" lets the sound server determine buffers.
(default 100)

option.name: --pulse-host
tip: Specify the host to use.
An empty <host> string uses a local connection, "localhost" uses network transfer (most likely not what you want).

option.name: --pulse-latency-hacks
tip: Enable hacks to workaround PulseAudio timing bugs (default: yes).
If enabled, mpv will do elaborate latency calculations on its own.
If disabled, it will use PulseAudio automatically updated timing information.
Disabling this might help with e.g. networked audio or some plugins, while enabling it might help in some unknown situations (it is currently enabled due to known bugs with PulseAudio 16.0).

option.name: --quiet
tip: Make console output less verbose; in particular, prevents the status line (i.e. AV: 3.4 (00:00:03.37) / 5320.6 ...) from being displayed.
Particularly useful on slow terminals or broken ones which do not properly handle carriage return (i.e. \r).
(default no)

option.name: --rar-list-all-volumes
tip: When opening multi-volume rar files, open all volumes to create a full list of contained files (default: no).
If disabled, only the archive entries whose headers are located within the first volume are listed (and thus played when opening a .rar file with mpv).
Doing so speeds up opening, and the typical idiotic use-case of playing uncompressed multi-volume rar files that contain a single media file is made faster.

option.name: --really-quiet
tip: Display even less output and status messages than with --quiet.
(default no)

option.name: --rebase-start-time
tip: Whether to move the file start time to 00:00:00 (default: yes).
This is less awkward for files which start at a random timestamp, such as transport streams.
On the other hand, if there are timestamp resets, the resulting behavior can be rather weird.
For this reason, and in case you are actually interested in the real timestamps, this behavior can be disabled with no.

option.name: --referrer
tip: Specify a referrer path or URL for HTTP requests.

option.name: --replaygain
tip: Adjust volume gain according to replaygain values stored in the file metadata.
With --replaygain=no (the default), perform no adjustment.
With --replaygain=track, apply track gain.
With --replaygain=album, apply album gain if present and fall back to track gain otherwise.

option.name: --replaygain-clip
tip: Allow the volume gain to clip (default: no).
If this option is not enabled, mpv automatically will prevent clipping by lowering the gain.

option.name: --replaygain-fallback
tip: Gain in dB to apply if the file has no replay gain tags.
This option is always applied if the replaygain logic is somehow inactive.
If this is applied, no other replaygain options are applied.
(default 0)

option.name: --replaygain-preamp
tip: Pre-amplification gain in dB to apply to the selected replaygain gain (default: 0).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file
tip: Normally, mpv will try to keep all settings when playing the next file on the playlist, even if they were changed by the user during playback. (This behavior is the opposite of MPlayer's, which tries to reset all settings when starting next file.)

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-pre
tip: Prepend 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --reset-on-next-file-toggle
tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --resume-playback
tip: Restore playback position from the watch_later configuration subdirectory, usually ~/.config/mpv/watch_later/ (default: yes).

option.name: --resume-playback-check-mtime
tip: Only restore the playback position from the watch_later configuration subdirectory (usually ~/.config/mpv/watch_later/) if the file's modification time is the same as at the time of saving.
This may prevent skipping forward in files with the same name which have different content. (Default: no)

option.name: --rtsp-transport
tip: Select RTSP transport method (default: tcp).
This selects the underlying network transport when playing rtsp://... URLs.
The value lavf leaves the decision to libavformat.

option.name: --saturation
tip: Adjust the saturation of the video signal (default: 0).
You can get grayscale output with this option.
Not supported by all video output drivers.

option.name: --save-position-on-quit
tip: Always save the current playback position on quit, and also when the loadfile command is used to replace the current playlist.
When this file is played again later, the player will seek to the old playback position on start.
This does not happen if playback of a file is stopped in other ways.
For example, going to the next file in the playlist will not save the position, and will start playback at beginning the next time the file is played.
(default no)

option.name: --save-watch-history
tip: Whether to save which files are played.
These can be then selected with the default g-h key binding.

option.name: --scale
tip: The filter function to use when upscaling video.

Possible values: bilinear, bicubic_fast, oversample, spline16, spline36, spline64, sinc, lanczos, ginseng, bicubic, hermite, catmull_rom, mitchell, robidoux, robidouxsharp, box, nearest, triangle, gaussian, jinc, ewa_lanczos, ewa_hanning, ewa_ginseng, ewa_lanczossharp, ewa_lanczos4sharpest, ewa_lanczossoft, haasnsoft, ewa_robidoux, ewa_robidouxsharp, bartlett, cosine, hanning, tukey, hamming, quadric, welch, kaiser, blackman, sphinx.
(default lanczos)

option.name: --scale-antiring
tip: Set the antiringing strength.
This tries to eliminate ringing, but can introduce other artifacts in the process.
Must be a float number between 0.0 and 1.0.
The default value of 0.0 disables antiringing entirely.

option.name: --scale-blur
tip: Kernel scaling factor (also known as a blur factor).
Decreasing this makes the result sharper, increasing it makes it blurrier (default 0).
If set to 0, the kernel's preferred blur factor is used.
Note that setting this too low (eg.
0.5) leads to bad results.
It's generally recommended to stick to values between 0.8 and 1.2.

option.name: --scale-clamp
tip: Specifies a weight bias to multiply into negative coefficients.
Specifying --scale-clamp=1 has the effect of removing negative weights completely, thus effectively clamping the value range to [0-1].
Values between 0.0 and 1.0 can be specified to apply only a moderate diminishment of negative weights.

This is especially useful for --tscale, where it reduces excessive ringing artifacts in the temporal domain (which typically manifest themselves as short flashes or fringes of black, mostly around moving edges) in exchange for potentially adding more blur.
The default for --tscale-clamp is 1.0, the others default to 0.0.

option.name: --scale-param1
tip: Set filter parameters.
By default, these are set to the special string default, which maps to a scaler-specific default value.
Ignored if the filter is not tunable.
Currently, this affects the following filter parameters:

option.name: --scale-param2
tip: Set filter parameters.
By default, these are set to the special string default, which maps to a scaler-specific default value.
Ignored if the filter is not tunable.
Currently, this affects the following filter parameters:

option.name: --scale-radius
tip: Set radius for tunable filters, must be a float number between 0.5 and 16.0.
Defaults to the filter's preferred radius if not specified.
Doesn't work for every scaler and VO combination.

option.name: --scale-taper
tip: Kernel/window taper factor.
Increasing this flattens the filter function.
Value range is 0 to 1.
A value of 0 (the default) means no flattening, a value of 1 makes the filter completely flat (equivalent to a box function).
Values in between mean that some portion will be flat and the actual filter function will be squeezed into the space in between.

option.name: --scale-window
tip: (Advanced users only) Choose a custom windowing function for the kernel.
Defaults to the filter's preferred window if unset.
Use --scale-window=help to get a list of supported windowing functions.
Possible values: bartlett, cosine, hanning, tukey, hamming, quadric, welch, kaiser, blackman, sphinx, jinc.

option.name: --scale-wparam
tip: (Advanced users only) Configure the parameter for the window function given by --scale-window etc.
By default, these are set to the special string default, which maps to a window-specific default value.
Ignored if the window is not tunable.
Currently, this affects the following window parameters:

option.name: --scale-wtaper
tip: Kernel/window taper factor.
Increasing this flattens the filter function.
Value range is 0 to 1.
A value of 0 (the default) means no flattening, a value of 1 makes the filter completely flat (equivalent to a box function).
Values in between mean that some portion will be flat and the actual filter function will be squeezed into the space in between.

option.name: --scaler-resizes-only
tip: Disable the scaler if the video image is not resized.
In that case, bilinear is used instead of whatever is set with --scale.
Bilinear will reproduce the source image perfectly if no scaling is performed.
Enabled by default.
Note that this option never affects --cscale.

option.name: --screen
tip: In multi-monitor configurations (i.e. a single desktop that spans across multiple displays), this option tells mpv which screen to display the video on.
(default default)

option.name: --screen-name
tip: In multi-monitor configurations, this option tells mpv which screen to display the video on based on the screen name from the video backend.
The same caveats in the --screen option also apply here.
This option is ignored and does nothing if --screen is explicitly set.

option.name: --screenshot-avif-encoder
tip: Specify the AV1 encoder to be used by libavcodec for encoding avif screenshots.
(default libaom-av1)

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts
tip: Specifies libavcodec options for selected encoder.
For more information, consult the FFmpeg documentation.
(default usage=allintra,crf=0,cpu-used=8)

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --screenshot-avif-opts-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --screenshot-avif-pixfmt
tip: Specify the pixel format for the libavcodec encoder.
Defaults to empty, which lets mpv pick one close to the source format.

option.name: --screenshot-directory
tip: Store screenshots in this directory.
This path is joined with the filename generated by --screenshot-template.
If the template filename is already absolute, the directory is ignored.

option.name: --screenshot-format
tip: Set the image file type used for saving screenshots.
Possible values: jpg, jpeg, png, webp, jxl, avif.
(default jpg)

option.name: --screenshot-high-bit-depth
tip: If possible, write screenshots with a bit depth similar to the source video (default: yes).
This is interesting in particular for PNG, as this sometimes triggers writing 16 bit PNGs with huge file sizes.
This will also include an unused alpha channel in the resulting files if 16 bit is used.

option.name: --screenshot-jpeg-quality
tip: Set the JPEG quality level.
Higher means better quality.
The default is 90.

option.name: --screenshot-jpeg-source-chroma
tip: Write JPEG files with the same chroma subsampling as the video (default: yes).
If disabled, the libjpeg default is used.

option.name: --screenshot-jxl-distance
tip: Set the JPEG XL Butteraugli distance.
Lower means better quality.
Lossless is 0.0, and 1.0 is approximately equivalent to JPEG quality 90 for photographic content.
Use 0.1 for "visually lossless" screenshots.
The default is 1.0.

option.name: --screenshot-jxl-effort
tip: Set the JPEG XL compression effort.
Higher effort (usually) means better compression, but takes more CPU time.
The default is 4.

option.name: --screenshot-png-compression
tip: Set the PNG compression level.
Higher means better compression.
This will affect the file size of the written screenshot file and the time it takes to write a screenshot.
Too high compression might occupy enough CPU time to interrupt playback.
The default is 7.

option.name: --screenshot-png-filter
tip: Set the filter applied prior to PNG compression.
0 is none, 1 is "sub", 2 is "up", 3 is "average", 4 is "Paeth", and 5 is "mixed".
This affects the level of compression that can be achieved.
For most images, "mixed" achieves the best compression ratio, hence it is the default.

option.name: --screenshot-sw
tip: Whether to use software rendering for screenshots (default: no).

option.name: --screenshot-tag-colorspace
tip: Tag screenshots with the appropriate colorspace (default: yes).

option.name: --screenshot-template
tip: Specify the filename template used to save screenshots.
The template specifies the filename without file extension, and can contain format specifiers, which will be substituted when taking a screenshot.
By default, the template is mpv-shot%n, which results in filenames like mpv-shot0012.png for example.

option.name: --screenshot-webp-compression
tip: Set the WebP compression level.
Higher means better compression, but takes more CPU time.
Note that this also affects the screenshot quality when used with lossy WebP files.
The default is 4.

option.name: --screenshot-webp-lossless
tip: Write lossless WebP files. --screenshot-webp-quality is ignored if this is set.
The default is no.

option.name: --screenshot-webp-quality
tip: Set the WebP quality level.
Higher means better quality.
The default is 75.

option.name: --script-opts
tip: Set options for scripts.
A script can query an option by key.
If an option is used and what semantics the option value has depends entirely on the loaded scripts.
Values not claimed by any scripts are ignored.

option.name: --script-opts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --script-opts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --script-opts-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

option.name: --script-opts-del
tip: Delete 1 or more items if present (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --script-opts-remove
tip: Delete item if present (no escapes).

option.name: --script-opts-set
tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

option.name: --scripts
tip: Load a Lua script.
The second option allows you to load multiple scripts by separating them with the path separator (: on Unix, ; on Windows).

option.name: --scripts-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --scripts-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --sdr-adjust-gamma
tip: SDR transfer functions are often ambiguous or mismatched.
Even if files are tagged with a specific function (e.g. bt.709), the actual content may not match.
For example, most screen capture software tags its output as bt.709, but the content is usually a direct sRGB capture.
(default auto)

option.name: --secondary-sid
tip: Select a secondary subtitle stream.
This is similar to --sid.
If a secondary subtitle is selected, it will be rendered as toptitle (i.e. on the top of the screen) alongside the normal subtitle by default, and provides a way to render two subtitles at once.

option.name: --secondary-sub-ass-override
tip: Control whether user secondary substyle overrides should be applied.
This works exactly like --sub-ass-override.
(default strip)

option.name: --secondary-sub-delay
tip: Delays secondary subtitles by <sec> seconds.
Can be negative.
(default 0)

option.name: --secondary-sub-pos
tip: Specify the position of secondary subtitles on the screen.
This is similar to --sub-pos but for secondary subtitles.
(default 0)

option.name: --secondary-sub-visibility
tip: Can be used to disable display of secondary subtitles, but still select and decode them.
(default yes)

option.name: --sharpen
tip: If set to a value other than 0, enable an unsharp masking filter.
Positive values will sharpen the image (but add more ringing and aliasing).
Negative values will blur the image.
If your GPU is powerful enough, consider alternatives like the ewa_lanczossharp scale filter, or the --scale-blur option. (Only for --vo=gpu)
(default 0)

option.name: --show-in-taskbar
tip: (Windows and X11 only) Show mpv in the taskbar (default: yes).
If set to no, mpv will no longer appear in taskbars and tasklists in supported window managers, and may be excluded from Alt+Tab window switching.

option.name: --show-profile
tip: Show the description and content of a profile.
Lists all profiles if no parameter is provided.

option.name: --shuffle
tip: Play files in random order.
(default no)

option.name: --sigmoid-center
tip: The center of the sigmoid curve used for --sigmoid-upscaling, must be a float between 0.0 and 1.0.
Defaults to 0.75 if not specified.

option.name: --sigmoid-slope
tip: The slope of the sigmoid curve used for --sigmoid-upscaling, must be a float between 1.0 and 20.0.
Defaults to 6.5 if not specified.

option.name: --sigmoid-upscaling
tip: When upscaling, use a sigmoidal color transform to avoid emphasizing ringing artifacts.
Enabled by default.
This is incompatible with and replaces --linear-upscaling. (Note that sigmoidization also requires linearization, so the LINEAR rendering step fires in both cases)

option.name: --slang
tip: Analogous to --alang, for subtitle tracks.

option.name: --slang-add
tip: Append 1 or more items (same syntax as -set).

option.name: --slang-append
tip: Append a single item (no escapes).

option.name: --slang-clr
tip: Clear the option (remove all items).

tip: Set a list of items (comma-separated, backslash escapes).

tip: Append an item, or remove it if it already exists (no escapes).

option.name: --snap-window
tip: (Windows only) Snap the player window to screen edges.
(default no)

option.name: --speed
tip: Slow down or speed up playback by the factor given as parameter.
(default 1)

option.name: --spirv-compiler
tip: Controls which compiler is used to translate GLSL to SPIR-V.
This is only relevant for --gpu-api=d3d11 with --vo=gpu.
Possible values: auto.
(default auto)

option.name: --sstep
tip: Skip <sec> seconds after every frame.
(default 0)

option.name: --start
tip: Seek to given time position.
(default none)

option.name: --stop-playback-on-init-failure
tip: Stop playback if either audio or video fails to initialize (default: no).
With no, playback will continue in video-only or audio-only mode if one of them fails.
This doesn't affect playback of audio-only or video-only files.

option.name: --stop-screensaver
tip: Turns off the screensaver (or screen blanker and similar mechanisms) at startup and turns it on again on exit (default: yes).
When using yes, the screensaver will re-enable when playback is not active. always will always disable the screensaver.
Note that stopping the screensaver is only possible if a video output is available (i.e. there is an open mpv window).
This is not supported on all video outputs, platforms, or desktop environments.

option.name: --stream-buffer-size
tip: Size of the low level stream byte buffer (default: 128KB).
This is used as buffer between demuxer and low level I/O (e.g. sockets).
Generally, this can be very small, and the main purpose is similar to the internal buffer FILE in the C standard library will have.

option.name: --stream-dump
tip: Instead of playing a file, read its byte stream and write it to the given destination file.
The destination is overwritten.
Can be useful to test network-related behavior.

option.name: --stream-lavf-o
tip: Set AVOptions on streams opened with libavformat.
Unknown or misspelled options are silently ignored. (They are mentioned in the terminal output in verbose mode, i.e. --v.
In general we can't print errors, because other options such as e.g. user agent are not available with all protocols, and printing errors for unknown options would end up being too noisy.)

tip: Write received/read data from the demuxer to the given output file.
The output file will always be overwritten without asking.
The output format is determined by the extension of the output file.

option.name: --stretch-dvd-subs
tip: Stretch DVD subtitles when playing anamorphic videos for better looking fonts on badly mastered DVDs.
This switch has no effect when the video is stored with square pixels - which for DVD input cannot be the case though.
(default no)

option.name: --stretch-image-subs-to-screen
tip: Stretch DVD and other image subtitles to the screen, ignoring the video margins.

This has a similar effect as --sub-use-margins for text subtitles, except that the text itself will be stretched, not only just repositioned. (At least in general it is unavoidable, as an image bitmap can in theory consist of a single bitmap covering the whole screen, and the player won't know where exactly the text parts are located.)
(default no)

option.name: --sub
tip: Display the subtitle stream specified by <ID>. auto selects the default, no disables subtitles.

option.name: --sub-align-x
tip: Control to which corner of the screen text subtitles should be aligned to (default: center).

option.name: --sub-align-y
tip: Vertical position (default: bottom).
Details see --sub-align-x.

option.name: --sub-ass
tip: Render ASS subtitles natively (default: yes).

option.name: --sub-ass-force-margins
tip: Enables placing toptitles and subtitles in black borders when they are available, if the subtitles are in the ASS format.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-ass-hinting
tip: Set font hinting type. <type> can be:
(default none)
(deprecated alias: --sub-ass-hinting)

option.name: --sub-ass-justify
tip: Applies justification as defined by --sub-justify on ASS subtitles if --sub-ass-override is not set to no.
Default: no.

option.name: --sub-ass-line-spacing
tip: Set line spacing value for SSA/ASS renderer.
(default 0)
(deprecated alias: --sub-ass-line-spacing)

option.name: --sub-ass-override
tip: Control whether user style overrides should be applied.
Note that all of these overrides try to be somewhat smart about figuring out whether or not a subtitle is considered a "sign" and try to be as non-destructive as possible.
(default scale)

option.name: --sub-ass-prune-delay
tip: Set the delay for automatic pruning of events from memory in libass.
When enabled, subtitle events are removed from memory once their end timestamp is older than the specified delay.
(default -1)

option.name: --sub-ass-scale-with-window
tip: Like --sub-scale-with-window, but affects subtitles in ASS format only.
Like --sub-scale, this can break ASS subtitles.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-ass-shaper
tip: Set the text layout engine used by libass.
(default complex)

tip: Load all SSA/ASS styles found in the specified file and use them for rendering text subtitles.
The syntax of the file is exactly like the [V4 Styles] / [V4+ Styles] section of SSA/ASS.

option.name: --sub-ass-use-video-data
tip: Controls which information about the video stream is passed to libass.
Any option but all is incompatible with standard ASS as defined by VSFilter, whose behavior most subtitle scripts and renderers target, including libass.
Video stream properties are needed to accurately emulate VSFilter semantics and withholding them will likely result in broken subtitle rendering for most files.
It's thus recommended to only change this selectively if required on a per-file basis.
(default all)

option.name: --sub-ass-video-aspect-override
tip: Allows passing any arbitrary aspect ratio to libass instead of the video’s actual aspect ratio.
Zero aspect ratio is identical to no.
(default 0)

option.name: --sub-ass-vsfilter-color-compat
tip: Mangle colors like (xy-)vsfilter do (default: basic).
Historically, VSFilter was not color space aware.
This was no problem as long as the color space used for SD video (BT.601) was used.

But when everything switched to HD (BT.709), VSFilter was still converting RGB colors to BT.601, rendered them into the video frame, and handled the frame to the video output, which would use BT.709 for conversion to RGB.
The result were mangled subtitle colors.
Later on, bad hacks were added on top of the ASS format to control how colors are to be mangled.

option.name: --sub-auto
tip: Load additional subtitle files matching the video filename.
The parameter specifies how external subtitle files are matched. exact is enabled by default.

option.name: --sub-auto-exts
tip: Subtitle extensions to try and match when using --sub-auto.
Note that modifying this list will also affect what mpv recognizes as subtitles when using drag and drop.
(default ass,idx,lrc,mks,pgs,rt,sbv,scc,smi,srt,ssa,sub,sup,utf,utf-8,utf8,vtt)

tip: Set the maximum bitmap cache size in libass cache for the subtitle track.
0 means libass uses its default value.
This accepts values in MB.

option.name: --sub-blur
tip: Gaussian blur factor applied to the sub font border.
0 means no blur applied (default).

option.name: --sub-bold
tip: Format text on bold.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-border-style
tip: The style of the border.
(default outline-and-shadow)

option.name: --sub-clear-on-seek
tip: (Obscure, rarely useful.) Can be used to play broken mkv files with duplicate ReadOrder fields.
ReadOrder is the first field in a Matroska-style ASS subtitle packets.
It should be unique, and libass uses it for fast elimination of duplicates.
This option disables caching of subtitles across seeks, so after a seek libass can't eliminate subtitle packets with the same ReadOrder as earlier packets.
Note that enabling this option can result in broken subtitle behavior if you are not actually playing one of the aforementioned broken mkv files.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-codepage
tip: You can use this option to specify the subtitle codepage. uchardet will be used to guess the charset. (If mpv was not compiled with uchardet, then utf-8 is the effective default.)

option.name: --sub-color
tip: Specify the color used for unstyled text subtitles.
(default #FFFFFFFF)

option.name: --sub-create-cc-track
tip: For every video stream, create a closed captions track (default: no).
The only purpose is to make the track available for selection at the start of playback, instead of creating it lazily.
This applies only to ATSC A53 Part 4 Closed Captions (displayed by mpv as subtitle tracks using the codec eia_608).
The CC track is marked "default" and selected according to the normal subtitle track selection rules.
You can then use --sid to explicitly select the correct track too.

option.name: --sub-delay
tip: Delays primary subtitles by <sec> seconds.
Can be negative.
(default 0)

option.name: --sub-demuxer
tip: Force subtitle demuxer type for --sub-file.
Give the demuxer name as printed by --sub-demuxer=help.

option.name: --sub-file-paths
tip: Specify extra directories to search for subtitles matching the video.
Multiple directories can be separated by ":" (";" on Windows).
Paths can be relative or absolute.
Relative paths are interpreted relative to video file directory.
If the file is a URL, only absolute paths and sub configuration subdirectory will be scanned.

tip: Whether to enable regex filtering (default: yes).
Note that if no regexes are added to the --sub-filter-regex list, setting this option to yes has no effect.
It's meant to easily disable or enable filtering temporarily.

option.name: --sub-filter-regex-plain
tip: Whether to first convert the ASS "Text" field to plain-text (default: no).
This strips ASS tags and applies ASS directives, like \N to new-line.
If the result is multi-line then the regexp anchors ^ and $ match each line, but still any match discards all lines.

tip: Applies filter removing subtitle additions for the deaf or hard-of-hearing (SDH).
This is intended for English, but may in part work for other languages too.
The intention is that it can be always enabled so may not remove all parts added.
(default no)

tip: Specify pairs of characters that --sub-filter-sdh will use to potentially remove text.
This is a string list option.
See List Options for details.
Text that is enclosed within each specified pair will be removed.
Note that parenthesis pairs (normal and full width) are treated as a special case and require --sub-fitler-sdh-harder to be removed.

tip: Do harder SDH filtering (if enabled by --sub-filter-sdh).
Will also remove speaker labels and text within parentheses using both lower and upper case letters.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-fix-timing
tip: Adjust subtitle timing is to remove minor gaps or overlaps between subtitles.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-fix-timing-keep
tip: Set the minimum duration in milliseconds for subtitle events to be considered for timing fixes (default: 400).
If a subtitle event has a duration smaller than this, its timing is not changed.

option.name: --sub-fix-timing-threshold
tip: Set the threshold in milliseconds for fixing subtitle timing (default: 210).
If the gap between two subtitle events is smaller than this, the gap is removed.

option.name: --sub-font
tip: Specify font to use for subtitles that do not themselves specify a particular font.
The default is sans-serif.

option.name: --sub-font-provider
tip: Which libass font provider backend to use (default: auto). auto will attempt to use the native font provider: fontconfig on Linux, CoreText on macOS, DirectWrite on Windows. fontconfig forces fontconfig, if libass was built with support (if not, it behaves like none).

option.name: --sub-font-size
tip: Specify the sub font size.
The unit is the size in scaled pixels at a window height of 720.
The actual pixel size is scaled with the window height: if the window height is larger or smaller than 720, the actual size of the text increases or decreases as well.
(default 38)

option.name: --sub-fonts-dir
tip: Font files in this directory are used by mpv/libass for subtitles.
Useful if you do not want to install fonts to your system.
Note that files in this directory are loaded into memory before being used by mpv.
If you have a lot of fonts, consider using fonts.conf (see FILES section) to include additional mpv user settings.

option.name: --sub-forced-events-only
tip: Enabling this displays only forced events within subtitle streams.
Only some bitmap subtitle formats (such as DVD or PGS) are capable of having a mixture of forced and unforced events within the stream.
Enabling this on text subtitles will cause no subtitles to be displayed (default: no).

option.name: --sub-fps
tip: Specify the framerate of the subtitle file (default: video fps).
Affects text subtitles only.

option.name: --sub-gauss
tip: Apply Gaussian blur to image subtitles (default: 0).
This can help to make pixelated DVD/Vobsubs look nicer.
A value other than 0 also switches to software subtitle scaling.
Might be slow.

option.name: --sub-glyph-limit
tip: Set the maximum number of cached glyphs in libass cache for the subtitle track.
0 means libass uses its default value.

option.name: --sub-gray
tip: Convert image subtitles to grayscale.
Can help to make yellow DVD/Vobsubs look nicer.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-hdr-peak
tip: Controls the text subtitle and OSD diffuse white level in cd/m² (nits) for HDR output (default: sdr). sdr is 203 cd/m² for standard SDR white. (--vo=gpu-next only)

option.name: --sub-italic
tip: Format text on italic.
(default no)

option.name: --sub-justify
tip: Control how multi line subs are justified irrespective of where they are aligned (default: auto which justifies as defined by --sub-align-x).
Left justification is recommended to make the subs easier to read as it is easier for the eyes.

option.name: --sub-lavc-o
tip: Pass AVOptions to libavcodec decoder.
Note, a patch to make the o= unneeded and pass all unknown options through the AVOption system is welcome.
A full list of AVOptions can be found in the FFmpeg manual.

tip: Top and bottom screen margin for the subs in scaled pixels (see --sub-font-size for details).
